options.rationale: Correct: KCL expresses conservation of charge at a node.

options.text: The sum of voltages around a loop is non-zero
options.rationale: KVL says loop voltages sum to zero, not KCL.

options.text: Current always flows from low to high voltage
options.rationale: Conventional current flows high to low potential through a resistor.
Resistance is voltage divided by current.

items.stem: Which TWO statements about power factor are correct? (Select TWO.)

options.text: It is the cosine of the phase angle between voltage and current
options.rationale: Correct: PF = cos(phi) for sinusoidal AC.

options.text: A low power factor means more current for the same real power
options.rationale: Correct: poor PF raises current and losses.

options.text: A power factor greater than 1 is desirable
Power factor applies only to DC circuits
options.rationale: Power factor is an AC concept.

items.stem: The time constant of an RC circuit is:

options.text: The product of resistance and capacitance
options.rationale: Correct: tau = RC sets how quickly the circuit charges or discharges.
The time constant is the product RC, not a ratio.

options.text: The supply voltage times the capacitance
options.rationale: That gives charge, not the time constant.
Resistance directly affects the time constant.
